title: Laredo's pediatric hospital push moves forward as advisory committee sets Dec. 8 meeting
excerpt: After more than 90 percent of voters backed expanding pediatric hospital services, Laredo's new Community Health Care Advisory Committee has held its first meeting and will take up the pediatric hospital question — including capacity and staffing — on Dec. 8.
content:
Efforts to expand pediatric hospital services in Laredo are moving into their next phase, with the city's new Community Health Care Advisory Committee holding its first meeting this month and planning to take up the pediatric hospital question at its next meeting on Tuesday, Dec. 8, according to KGNS.

More than 90 percent of voters supported a nonbinding proposition on Nov. 3 calling for efforts to expand pediatric hospital services in Laredo and Webb County. Mayor Victor Treviño proposed the measure in August, saying Laredo needs a pediatric hospital.

Laredo has no pediatric hospital, so families travel to San Antonio and Corpus Christi for children's care. Ray Sanchez, with the nonprofit Smiles From Heaven, told KGNS his family left Laredo for his daughter Bella's leukemia treatment, describing the travel as a strain on the family and an emotional toll on Bella, and called on the city, Webb County, nonprofits and others to work together.

The advisory committee took no action at its first meeting. At the Dec. 8 meeting it will discuss the health care workforce and specialty care, including pediatric services. Laredo Public Health Director Dr. Richard Chamberlain said the committee will discuss a pediatric hospital and its capacity and review data on the city's current health care landscape. Funding and staffing are still being discussed, and the committee plans to present data from its first 90 days of work to the City Council in April 2027.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 10, 2026; kgns.tv.
